Feluda.description: Prodosh C. Mitter, known as Feluda, is a private detective and the protagonist of the series, renowned for his keen observation and deductive skills.

Lalmohan Babu.description: Lalmohan Ganguly, a thriller writer under the pen name Jatayu and Feluda's friend, who is asked to play the film role of the villain's right-hand man, Aghorchand Batlivala.

Pulak Ghoshal.description: A film director who adapts Lalmohan Babu's stories into Hindi films and gives instructions regarding production and costumes.

Rajen Raina.description: A film actor playing the hero in Pulak Ghoshal's movie, recognized for his cheerful demeanor and seen signing autographs.

Mahadev Verma.description: A film actor cast as the villain in the movie, noted for his interesting appearance and mannerisms.

Suchandra.description: Suchandra is the heroine in Pulak Ghoshal's film, introduced in the film version though absent from the original story.

Birupaksha Majumdar.description: Birupaksha Majumdar is a retired managing director of Bengal Bank, a former sportsman and shikari, whose family owns a large villa in Darjeeling. He is often referred to as Mr Majumdar.

Srinath.description: Srinath is mentioned as the person who brings tea to the group.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, India, known for its tea plantations and scenic views of the Himalayas.

Karakoram.description: A mountain range spanning the borders of India, Pakistan, and China, famous for its rugged terrain and high peaks.

Bombay.description: Now called Mumbai, it is the capital city of Maharashtra and the center of India's film industry.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, historically significant and culturally rich, now divided into West Bengal (India) and Bangladesh.

Sunderbans.description: A vast mangrove forest in the delta region of Bengal, home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.

Ganga.description: The Ganges River, a major and sacred river in India.

Padma.description: A major river in Bangladesh, forming part of the Ganges delta.

Meghna.description: A river in Bangladesh, also part of the Ganges delta system.

Himalayas.description: The world's highest mountain range, spanning northern India and other countries.

Chandannagore.description: A town in West Bengal, India, known for its French colonial history.

Nayanpur.description: A place in East Bengal, referenced as the ancestral home of Birupaksha Majumdar's family.

Mount Everest Hotel.description: A hotel in Darjeeling where the film unit is staying.

Hotel Kanchenjunga.description: A hotel in Darjeeling, named after the third highest mountain in the world.

Bagdogra.description: A town in West Bengal, India, with an airport serving as the gateway to Darjeeling.

Leh.description: A town in Ladakh, northern India, known for its scenic beauty and Buddhist culture.

Ladakh.description: A region in northern India, famous for its mountains and unique culture.

Kashmir.description: A region in northern India, renowned for its natural beauty and historical significance.

Srinagar.description: The largest city in Kashmir, known for its lakes and gardens.

Bengal Bank.description: A bank referenced as Birupaksha Majumdar's former workplace.

kurta.description: A traditional long shirt worn in India, often made of cotton or silk.

Puja.description: Refers to Hindu religious festivals or rituals, commonly celebrated in Bengal during autumn.

shikari.description: A hunter; someone who engages in hunting, often used in Indian contexts.

Uncle Sidhu.description: A relative of Feluda and Topshe, known for his habit of collecting interesting newspaper clippings, not limited to crime.

Sonada.description: A small town near Darjeeling, mentioned as a stop on the journey.

Rajasthani.description: Relating to Rajasthan, a state in western India, referenced here in the context of a traditional cap.

Kerseong.description: A town near Darjeeling, known for its picturesque landscape and tea gardens.

Kanchenjunga.description: The third highest mountain in the world, visible from Darjeeling and a major attraction for visitors.

Ghoom.description: A small town near Darjeeling, famous for its railway station and monastery.

Bosepukur.description: A locality mentioned as the site of a previous case solved by Feluda.

Nayanpur Villa.description: The bungalow in Darjeeling where Mr Majumdar lives.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, the capital city of West Bengal, India.

Keventer’s.description: A well-known open-air restaurant in Darjeeling, famous for its food and beverages.

Charminar.description: A popular Indian cigarette brand, smoked by Feluda.

ABCD.description: An acronym for 'Asia’s Best Crime Detector', a playful title given to Feluda by Lalmohan Babu.

Rajat Bose.description: The son of Sudheer Brahma working as Mr Majumdar's secretary under an alias to seek revenge for his father's death.

Observatory Hill.description: A notable hill in Darjeeling, known for its scenic views.

Das Studio.description: A local photography studio in Darjeeling.

London.description: Capital city of the United Kingdom, referenced for newspaper cuttings.

Statesman.description: A well-known English-language newspaper in India.

Sherlock Holmes.description: Famous fictional detective created by Arthur Conan Doyle.

Hercule Poirot.description: Famous fictional detective created by Agatha Christie.

zamindar.description: A zamindar is a hereditary landowner, historically powerful in Bengal, who collected taxes and owned large estates. 'Zamindars' is the plural form.

Gorpar Friends’ Club.description: A local club referenced for a past play performance.

Bengali Club.description: A local club in Darjeeling, mentioned for providing actors.

shikar.description: Hunting, especially for sport, in the Indian context.

bearer.description: A servant or attendant, often responsible for serving food and drinks.

Harinarayan Mukherjee.description: Harinarayan Mukherjee is an elderly gentleman who lives next to Mr Majumdar's house and introduces himself to Feluda and his friends. He is also referred to as Mr Mukherjee.

North Calcutta.description: A region in Kolkata, referenced in relation to Lalmohan Babu's past achievements.

Nehru Road.description: A road named after Jawaharlal Nehru, leading towards the hotel.

The Retreat.description: The name of Harinarayan Mukherjee's house, located next to Mr Majumdar's.

Carrom.description: A popular tabletop game in South Asia, similar to billiards but played with disks.

ashtadhatu.description: A traditional alloy of eight metals, often used in making sacred statues in India.

Namaskar.description: A traditional Indian greeting, similar to 'hello' or 'greetings'.

Mr Nitish Som.description: A member of the film unit who comes to collect Lalmohan Babu for the film shoot.

Topshe.description: Feluda's younger cousin and the narrator of the story, who assists in the investigations.

Jalapahar Road.description: A road in Darjeeling, known for its scenic views.

The Mall.description: The Mall is the main promenade or public square in Darjeeling, popular for walks and shopping. It is sometimes referred to simply as 'Mall.'

mahurat.description: A traditional ceremony marking the auspicious beginning of a film shoot.

gumpha.description: A Buddhist monastery, often found in the Himalayan regions.

Samiran Majumdar.description: Samiran Majumdar is Mr Majumdar's son, a businessman involved with the share market, who is first to discover his father's body and assists in the investigation. He is also called Samiran or Samiran Babu.

Jatish Saha.description: Jatish Saha is the police inspector in charge of the investigation at Nayanpur Villa, known for his methodical and thorough questioning. He is also referred to as Inspector Saha.

Lokenath.description: The bearer at Nayanpur Villa, responsible for serving tea and other duties, now missing.

Bahadur.description: A servant living in Nayanpur Villa.

Sudev Ghosh.description: The cameraman of the film unit.

Birch Hill Road.description: A road in the vicinity, mentioned as part of the day's activities.

Trofnil.description: An anti-depressant medication, relevant to the murder investigation.

Krishna.description: A Hindu deity, whose statue made of ashtadhatu is stolen in the story.

Baba.description: A term for father in Bengali and Hindi.

vish.description: Hindi for 'poison', used in the victim's dying message.

Siliguri.description: A city in West Bengal, India, mentioned as a location where police are searching for Lokenath.

veranda.description: An open, roofed porch or gallery along the outside of a building, common in Indian architecture.

Raja Prithvi Singh.description: The Raja of Neelkanthapur, a royal figure who invited Birupaksha Majumdar for tiger hunting in Neelkanthapur.

Sudheer Brahma.description: A Bengali professor of history and ayurveda enthusiast who was accidentally killed during a tiger hunt.

Neelkanthapur.description: A place in Madhya Pradesh where the past tiger hunting incident occurred.

Madhya Pradesh.description: A large state in central India, the setting for part of the backstory.

Chhota Nagpur.description: A plateau region in eastern India, where Mukherjee lived for a few years.

machaan.description: A raised platform or watchtower used for hunting or observation, especially in forests.

ayurveda.description: An ancient Indian system of medicine focused on natural and holistic healing.

babu.description: A term of respect or endearment in India, especially Bengal, often used to address men. 'Babu' is the capitalized form, while 'babu' is the lowercase variant.

Ek minute thahariye, hum dekhte hain.description: Hindi for 'Wait a minute, we will see/check.'

Bahut, bahut shukriya.description: Hindi for 'Thank you very, very much.'

Dr Bardhan.description: A doctor at the clinic who examines Feluda and provides insights into Mr Majumdar's health and family issues.

Kanpur.description: A city in northern India where Rajat Bose spent his childhood.

Readers’ Digest.description: An international magazine mentioned as reading material by Rajat Bose.

Arjun Mehrotra.description: A film actor suggested as a replacement for Rajen Raina in Pulak Ghoshal's film.

Tung.description: Another small location near Darjeeling, passed during the chase.

Pankhabari.description: A region or shortcut route in the hills near Darjeeling.

Dum Dum airport.description: The main airport in Kolkata, referenced in relation to a scent Feluda remembers.

Simla.description: A hill station in northern India, considered as an alternate shooting location.

Asia.description: The continent referenced in the playful title 'Asia’s Busiest Cinema Director.'

bed tea.description: A cup of tea served in the morning, often in bed, a common practice in parts of India.

ch-8: Ek minute thahariye, hum dekhte hain
